---

# Message to a licensed Kosovo accountant — Aureon Global Sh.P.K.

**Subject:** Aureon Global Sh.P.K. — confirm CIT regime (QS vs QL/CD) before the 15 July quarterly deadline

---

Dear [Accountant name],

We are a Kosovo Sh.P.K. (LLC), Aureon Global, incorporated in 2026, providing B2B services. We have no employees, are not registered for VAT, and our gross turnover is currently well under EUR 30,000 for the year. Before the 15 July 2026 quarterly deadline I would like to engage you to confirm four points and tell us exactly what to file. Concise answers are fine.

1. **Which regime applies to us.** For an Sh.P.K. with gross annual income under EUR 30,000, do we file the presumptive quarterly turnover tax (the "small business" 3%/9% on gross), or is a limited liability company required to keep full books and pay the 10% profit CIT (quarterly advances plus the annual CD return) regardless of turnover? In short: is the presumptive regime available to a corporate entity, or only to individual businesses?

2. **Our rate, if presumptive.** If we do file on gross turnover, is our rate 3% or 9%? We provide services, which I understand falls under the 9% category, but I want this confirmed against our registered NACE / activity code. Our code is [insert NACE code from ARBK extract]. Please confirm the correct treatment and whether the EUR 37.50 quarterly minimum applies to us.

3. **Annual return under the presumptive regime.** If we are on the presumptive turnover tax, are we still required to file an annual CD return with financial statements, or only the four quarterly statements plus the year-end final settlement? I want to be clear on whether any annual filing falls due in early 2027 for our first financial year.

4. **Q1 2026 and nil filings.** Given we had little or no income in the first quarter, was any quarterly statement due by 15 April 2026? If so, is a nil filing required to keep us in good standing, and how do we correct it now if it was missed? Please also confirm the Q2 2026 statement is due 15 July 2026.

For context: we are not VAT-registered (turnover under the EUR 30,000 registration threshold), have no payroll, and have no rent, interest, royalty, or non-resident supplier payments that would trigger withholding. I can send you our ARBK extract, fiscal number, and the invoices issued to date as soon as you confirm you can take this on.

Could you confirm the above in writing, and let me know your fee for handling our quarterly and annual filings? I would like this settled before 15 July.

Thank you,

[Your name]
Aureon Global Sh.P.K.
[Phone] | info@aureonglobal.de

---

## Notes for you (not part of the message)

- **Why these four questions matter.** Kosovo's presumptive regime (3% on trade/transport/agriculture, 9% on services/professional, minimum EUR 37.50 per quarter) applies to taxpayers with gross annual income up to EUR 30,000. The open question is whether an **Sh.P.K. (a corporation)** may use it at all, or whether the presumptive 3%/9% is reserved for individual/natural-person businesses while every LLC must keep books and file the 10% CIT with the annual CD return. That is genuinely unsettled for your case and is exactly why point (1) leads. Source: [PwC Kosovo — Taxes on corporate income](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/kosovo/corporate/taxes-on-corporate-income).
- **One field to fill before sending:** your registered **NACE / activity code** in question 2 (from the ARBK extract). If you don't have it handy, drop the ARBK extract in the data-inbox and I'll insert it.
- **Quarterly payment timing.** Presumptive quarterly payments are due within 15 days of each quarter's close, so Q2 2026 lands on **15 July 2026** — consistent with the deadline you named. The final settlement for a presumptive taxpayer is due **31 March** of the following year. I've left both in the message for the accountant to confirm rather than asserting them as settled.
- **Boundary reminder:** I drafted this; I have not sent it. You approve and send from your own address.

---

---

## Additional question — May invoices and the fresh start

From 30 June 2026 we reorganised invoicing and bookkeeping (new compliant invoices, paid via Payoneer). Three invoices were issued to one client in May 2026 totalling EUR 1,500 (real income). Going forward we treat the books as starting from the new system. Question: must those May 2026 invoices still be declared on the Q2 2026 return, since they are real Q2 income, or may the Q2 return start only from the new-system invoices? We want to be sure we are not under-declaring.
